rationale:
Evidence: all 60 trials of iteration 2 ended off track. Progress was 0.115 on the oval, 0.040 on the s-bend and 0.035 on the slalom. The iteration 1 candidate (kd 0.30, sensors +/-0.04 m) was the best raced score (52.35), and its s-bend and slalom progress (0.157 and 0.110) were clearly higher than the kd 0.15 runs. So kd 0.15 is the most likely cause of the lost progress on those tracks. Iteration 2 also cut oval line-loss events from 1 to 0 with the wider +/-0.05 m sensor array, so that change is worth keeping. The oval still stalls at progress 0.115 with max_error 0.0614, just over the 0.06 m off-track limit, which suggests the robot enters the first corner too fast.

Changes, following the Evaluator's requests: (1) kd goes from 0.15 back to 0.30, the value that gave the only progress gains so far. (2) base_speed goes from 1.6 to 1.4, a single test of whether slower entry lets the oval hold the line. (3) The +/-0.05 m sensor spread, sensor size 0.012, weights, kp 4.0, ki 0.05 and line_loss last_direction are unchanged. I am not changing line_loss yet, because the Evaluator asked for that only if line-loss events stay at 1 on s-bend or slalom after this race.

Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress recover toward 0.15 and 0.11 or higher. Oval max_error falls below 0.06 with line-loss events at 0 or 1, and oval progress rises above 0.115. The cost is some steering oscillation, which was 0.154 and 0.158 at kd 0.30 in iteration 1; that is a guide, not a score term.

Hypotheses and next measurements: (a) base_speed 1.4 with kd 0.30 gives oval max_error below 0.06 and oval progress above 0.115. (b) s-bend and slalom progress are at or above iteration 1 values. (c) steering_oscillation stays near 0.15. If oval progress still stalls at 0.115, next test sensor_size 0.016 or a different line_loss search direction. If s-bend or slalom still show one line-loss event, test line_loss search_right or search_left, with all other fields fixed.
